# Timeline

79 tools for Level Sequences with their bindings, tracks, sections and keyframes, camera cuts and shots, playback, and Blueprint timelines.

Back to the [index](README.md).

## `add_attach_track`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add a Sequencer 3D-Attach track on a binding so it follows another binding (e.g. a prop attached to a character's hand socket) over the section's range.  The attachee binding owns a UMovieScene3DAttachTrack; AddConstraint creates an attach section pointing at the target binding.  Idempotent by (target_binding_guid, start_frame).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding to attach (the attachee; this binding owns the attach track). |
| `target_binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding to attach TO (the parent/target). |
| `start_frame` | number | no | Optional start frame of the attach section (default: the sequence playback range start). |
| `duration` | number | no | Optional duration in frames (default: the playback range size). |
| `socket_name` | string | no | Optional socket name on the target to attach to (default: none -> target root). |
| `component_name` | string | no | Optional component name on the target to attach to (default: none). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, target_binding_guid: string, track_added: bool, already_exists: bool, start_frame: int, duration: int, socket_name: string, component_name: string, section_count: int, track_class: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_audio_section`

*Additive.*

Adds (or reuses) a root audio track on a Level Sequence and optionally a section.  Finds an existing root UMovieSceneAudioTrack or adds one. If sound_path loads a USoundBase, a sound section is placed at the playback range start.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `sound_path` | string | no | Optional content path of a USoundBase, e.g. "/Game/Audio/MySound". |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, track_class: string, audio_track: string, audio_track_index: int (the index set_audio_section_properties takes), track_added: bool, sound_loaded: bool, section_added: bool, section_count: int, sound_path: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_camera_cut`

*Additive.*

Adds a camera cut section bound to a camera binding over a frame range, creating the camera cut track if it does not yet exist, then saves the sequence. The binding must exist in the sequence (get_sequence_bindings lists them), or nothing is added.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence (first asset under /Game with that name), or its full /Game path. |
| `camera_binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the camera binding the cut switches to. |
| `sequence_path` | string | no | Alias of sequence_name. |
| `start_frame` | number | no | Optional inclusive start frame in tick resolution (default 0). |
| `end_frame` | number | no | Optional exclusive end frame (default start_frame + 1); must be > start_frame. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, sequence_path: string, camera_binding_guid: string, start_frame: int, end_frame: int, track_class: string, section_class: string, section_index: int, section_count: int, section_added: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_camera_cut_track`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add the camera cut track of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match), the root track whose sections pick the camera the sequence shows, in one undo step, then save the sequence. A movie scene holds at most one: when it already has one, nothing is added, written or saved (track_added false, changed false, saved false), so a repeat call is idempotent, and a camera cut track of another class there is an error. A new track has no section. A missing sequence is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Cuts: add_camera_cut; a camera with its cut: create_cine_camera_in_sequence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_count: int, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `add_component_material_track`

*Additive.*

Adds a component material parameter track for one indexed material slot to an object binding of a Level Sequence (first asset-name match under /Game), or reuses the binding's existing track for that slot, and saves the sequence. With parameter_name it keys that scalar parameter at frame (a tick-resolution frame) and reads the key back: success requires it, and a key the engine would skip (locked section, read-only sequence) is refused before anything is written; without it, it only adds a section spanning the playback range when the track has none. The slot index is not checked against the bound component, which is not resolved. An unknown binding_guid or a material_index that is not a whole number >= 0 is an error. For a Material Parameter Collection use add_material_parameter_collection_track; for other animated properties use add_property_track.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the actor/component object binding to attach the material track to |
| `material_index` | number | no | Optional indexed material slot the track animates, a whole number >= 0 (default 0) |
| `parameter_name` | string | no | Optional scalar material parameter name to key |
| `value` | number | no | Optional scalar value for the keyed parameter (default 0.0) |
| `frame` | number | no | Optional frame number for the key (default 0) |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, material_index: int, material_type: string, parameter_name: string, value: number, key_added: bool (read back from the track), section_added: bool (the track gained a section, keying included), scalar_channel_count: int, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_event_track_to_sequence`

*Additive.*

Add a new root event track (UMovieSceneEventTrack) to a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match), in one undo step, then save the sequence. Every call adds another track, even when the sequence already has one, and the new track has no sections (section_count 0). Add trigger sections with add_event_track_section, which appends to the first event track of the sequence. A sequence that is not found is an error; a failed save (for example during PIE) makes success false with saved=false and save_error. List root tracks with get_sequence_tracks; the inverse is remove_sequence_track; for a fade track use add_fade_track_to_sequence.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, track_class: string, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_fade_track_to_sequence`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Add the root fade track of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match), with a fade section spanning the playback range, in one undo step, then save the sequence. A fade track already there is reused and gets a section only when it has none, so a repeat call is idempotent: a fade track that already has a section is left as it is, with nothing written or saved (track_added and section_added false, changed false, saved false). A missing sequence is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. List root tracks with get_sequence_tracks; inverse: remove_sequence_track.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, section_count: int, section_class: string, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `add_keyframe_to_property_track`

*Additive.*

Adds a keyframe to a property track's section channel(s) at the given time, in one undo step, then saves the sequence. The property track must already exist (call add_property_track first); property_name picks which one when the binding has several tracks of that type. The value is keyed onto every channel of the section. By default a key already at that tick frame is updated in place; interp_mode (float/vector/color tracks only) instead INSERTS a key with that interpolation -- linear, constant, or cubic with explicit broken arrive_tangent/leave_tangent -- even on an occupied frame. Read keys back with get_channel_keyframes, retime one with move_keyframe.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding owning the property track. |
| `property_type` | string | yes | One of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility". |
| `time_seconds` | number | yes | Time (seconds, >= 0) at which to place the key; rounded to the nearest tick frame. |
| `property_name` | string | no | Optional name or path of the property whose track takes the key, case ignored; omitted, the first track of property_type on the binding. A name no track of that type animates is an error that lists the ones it does. |
| `value` | any | no | Key value. For Float: a scalar. For Bool/Visibility: a bool. For Vector/Color: a list of numbers (Vector/Color). Defaults to 0 / [] if omitted. |
| `interp_mode` | string | no | Optional, float channels only: "cubic", "linear" or "constant". When given the key is inserted with that interpolation instead of updating one at that frame. |
| `arrive_tangent` | number | no | Optional tangent for interp_mode "cubic" (default 0). |
| `leave_tangent` | number | no | Optional tangent for interp_mode "cubic" (default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, property_type: string, property_name: string, time_seconds: float, key_frame: int, keys_added: int, channel_count: int, key_index: int, key_count: int, interp_mode?: string, arrive_tangent?: float, leave_tangent?: float, saved: bool, save_error?: string } -- key_index and key_count describe the section's first channel; property_name is the property of the track that took the key.`

## `add_level_visibility_track`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Add a root level-visibility track (UMovieSceneLevelVisibilityTrack) to a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, or reuse the one it has, give it a section spanning the playback range when it has none, and set that section's streamed-level visibility, in one undo step, then save the sequence. Idempotent: a repeat call reuses the track and its first section and overwrites their visibility, and their level names when level_names is non-empty, with the values passed; visible defaults to true, so omitting it sets an existing section back to Visible. A missing sequence is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. For an actor's own visibility use add_property_track (property_type=Visibility, property_name=bVisible); list root tracks with get_sequence_tracks; the inverse is remove_sequence_track.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case. |
| `visible` | boolean | no | Optional bool, default true (levels Visible); false makes them Hidden. Written on every call. |
| `level_names` | array | no | Optional array of streamed-level short names the section controls, e.g. ["Sublevel_Interior"]; a non-empty array overwrites the section's list, an empty or omitted one keeps it. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, section_count: int, section_class: string, visibility: string, level_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_marked_frame`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Adds a marked frame (a labelled marker on the Sequencer timeline) at a tick-resolution frame of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, in one undo step, and saves the sequence; is_determinism_fence turns the same mark into an evaluation fence. Idempotent per frame: an existing mark at that frame is updated instead of duplicated, its label replaced when one is given and both flags overwritten with the values passed (false when omitted); already_existed says which. When the mark already has both flags and the label given (or no label is given), the call changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false). Read marks with get_marked_frames, delete one with remove_marked_frame.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `frame` | number | yes | Tick frame number to mark. |
| `label` | string | no | Optional human-readable label (auto-generated if empty). |
| `is_determinism_fence` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false): treat the mark as an evaluation fence (cannot be crossed in one evaluation). |
| `is_inclusive` | boolean | no | Optional bool (default false): when a determinism fence, how the previous/next ranges are dissected ((X,Y]->(Y,Z] vs (X,Y)->[Y,Z]). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, frame: int, mark_index: int, label: string, is_determinism_fence: bool, is_inclusive: bool, already_existed: bool, marked_frame_count: int, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `add_material_parameter_collection_track`

*Additive.*

Add a Material Parameter Collection root track bound to an existing MPC asset to a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, or reuse its MPC track already bound to that collection, in one undo step, then save the sequence. With parameter_name it keys that scalar parameter at frame (a tick-resolution frame) with value, and key_added is read back: a key the engine skips (locked section, read-only sequence) leaves key_added false without failing the call. Without parameter_name it only gives the track a playback-range section when it has none. The parameter name is not checked against the collection. A missing sequence or MPC is an error; a failed save makes success false. Component material slot: add_component_material_track; a new collection parameter: add_collection_parameter.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name (not a path) of the Level Sequence, e.g. "LS_Intro"; the first match under /Game is used, ignoring case. |
| `mpc_path` | string | yes | Object path of an existing UMaterialParameterCollection asset (e.g. /Game/MyGame/MPC_X) |
| `parameter_name` | string | no | Optional scalar parameter name to key on the MPC track; not checked against the collection. Omit it to add only the track and a section. |
| `value` | number | no | Optional scalar value for the keyed parameter (default 0.0) |
| `frame` | number | no | Optional key frame in the sequence's tick resolution, not display-rate frames (default 0); fractions are truncated. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, mpc_path: string, mpc_name: string, parameter_name: string, value: number, key_added: bool, section_added: bool, scalar_channel_count: int, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_property_track`

*Additive.*

Adds a typed property track + section to a Level Sequence binding.  The track animates a named property on the bound object (e.g. property_type Float with "Intensity", Visibility with "bVisible"). A section spanning the movie scene's playback range is created so keys evaluate.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence (found by AssetName under /Game), or its full /Game path. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of an existing binding (possessable or spawnable). |
| `property_type` | string | yes | One of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility". |
| `property_name` | string | yes | Name of the animated property (e.g. "RelativeLocation", "Intensity", "bHidden"). Used as both the property name and path. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, property_type: string, property_name: string, track_class: string, section_class: string, section_created: bool, section_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_sequence_folder`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Create a Sequencer outliner folder on a Level Sequence's movie scene (root folder, or a child of a named parent), inside an undo transaction, and save the sequence; success requires the save. Idempotent by name: a folder that already exists succeeds with already_existed true and saved false (nothing is written).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `folder_name` | string | yes | Name of the folder to create. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `parent_folder` | string | no | Optional name of an existing parent folder; if given, the new folder is nested under it instead of at the root. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, folder_name: string, parent_folder: string, created: bool, already_existed: bool, root_folder_count: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_shot_section`

*Additive.*

Adds a cinematic shot section (UMovieSceneCinematicShotSection) to the shot track and saves the sequence.  Creates the cinematic shot track if it does not exist yet. The inner shot sequence is shot_sequence_path, or &lt;target name>_Shot in the target's folder when omitted; it is loaded when it exists, else created and saved as a new asset (inner_sequence_created says which). An inner shot sequence that cannot be loaded, created or saved (a new one that fails to save stays in memory only), that is the target itself or that already plays it at any depth is an error and nothing is added. success is false, with save_error, when the save of the target fails.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `shot_sequence_path` | string | no | Optional content path of the inner shot Level Sequence. If omitted, an inner shot Level Sequence is created and persisted. |
| `start_frame` | number | no | Inclusive start frame for the shot section (default 0). |
| `duration` | number | no | Section duration in tick frames (default 150). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, inner_sequence_created: bool (true only when this call created the inner sequence), shot_name: string, shot_sequence_path: string, start_frame: int, duration: int, section_count: int, section_class: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_slomo_track`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Add the root time-dilation (slomo) track of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match), with a section spanning the playback range, and key dilation at frame, in one undo step, then save the sequence. A slomo track already there is reused with its first section; the key overwrites a key at that tick frame whole, interpolation included, or is added. A track whose section already holds that very key at that frame changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false), so a repeat call is idempotent. This is asset data, not the PIE player play rate. A missing sequence is an error; a failed save makes success false with saved=false and save_error. Change the key's interpolation with set_keyframe_interpolation.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence |
| `dilation` | number | no | Optional time-dilation multiplier (default 1.0; &lt;1 slower, >1 faster) |
| `frame` | number | no | Optional frame number for the dilation key (default 0) |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, section_count: int, section_class: string, dilation: number, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `add_subcomponent_possessable`

*Additive.*

Adds a component possessable as a child of an existing binding (possessable or spawnable) of a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, in an undo transaction, and saves the sequence; each call adds a new one, named possessable_name or else the component_class text. It records name, class and parent only: no component object is bound to it. To possess an actual component of an editor-world actor use bind_component_to_sequence; for whole actors use bind_actor_to_sequence or add_spawnable_to_sequence. An unknown parent GUID, an unresolvable class, or a class that is not an ActorComponent is an error.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the level sequence asset. |
| `parent_binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the parent binding (spawnable or possessable). |
| `component_class` | string | yes | Component class name (e.g. 'StaticMeshComponent', 'SpotLightComponent'). |
| `possessable_name` | string | no | Optional override name for the new possessable. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, possessable_guid: string, component_class: string, parent_guid: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `add_subsequence_track`

*Additive.*

Nests one Level Sequence in another: finds the target's first root track of exactly the subsequence class (never a cinematic shot track or another subclass) or adds one, adds a sub section playing the inner sequence from start_frame for duration tick-resolution frames, and saves the target. The inner sequence is sub_sequence_path, or &lt;target name>_Sub in the target's folder when omitted; it is loaded when it exists, else created and saved as a new asset (inner_sequence_created says which). Each call adds another section. An inner sequence that cannot be loaded, created or saved (a new one that fails to save stays in memory only), that is the target itself, or that already plays the target at any depth is an error and nothing is added. success is false, with save_error, when the save of the target fails. For cinematic shots use add_shot_track.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path (e.g. "/Game/MyGame/SUBSEQ_Example") OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `sub_sequence_path` | string | no | Optional content path of the sub Level Sequence to nest. If omitted, a sibling inner Level Sequence is created and persisted. |
| `start_frame` | number | no | Inclusive start frame for the sub section (default 0). |
| `duration` | number | no | Section duration in tick frames (default 150). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, track_class: string, track_added: bool, section_added: bool, inner_sequence_created: bool (true only when this call created the inner sequence), start_frame: int, duration: int, section_count: int, sub_sequence_path: string, sub_sequence_name: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `bind_actor_to_sequence`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Adds a possessable binding to a Level Sequence for an existing editor-world actor, and with property_name + property_type also adds a typed property track (with a section spanning the playback range) to it -- the bind+animate flow in one call. Idempotent per actor: an actor the sequence already possesses keeps its binding (binding_created false), and without a property to add nothing changes or is saved.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Label (or name) of the actor in the current editor world to possess. |
| `property_name` | string | no | Optional property of the actor to animate (e.g. "bHidden"); needs property_type. Used as both the property name and path. |
| `property_type` | string | no | Optional, with property_name: one of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility". |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, actor_name: string, binding_guid: string, display_name: string, possessable: bool, binding_created: bool, property_name?: string, property_type?: string, track_class?: string, section_class?: string, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string } -- the property fields only when a track was added.`

## `bind_component_to_sequence`

*Destructive.*

Adds a possessable binding for an actor's component to a Level Sequence, and with property_name + property_type also adds a typed property track (with a section spanning the playback range) to that new binding. Resolves the actor by label in the current editor world, finds the named component (by component name, class name, or "root"), adds a possessable for the component class, binds the component, and parents the component binding to the actor's binding when the actor is already possessed. Every call makes a NEW component possessable; when the track step fails the new binding stays.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `actor_name` | string | yes | Label (or name) of the actor in the current editor world. |
| `component_name` | string | yes | Component object name, component class name, or "root". |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `property_name` | string | no | Optional component property to animate (e.g. "Intensity"); needs property_type. Used as both property name and path, and not checked against the component. |
| `property_type` | string | no | Optional, with property_name: one of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility". |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, actor_name: string, component_name: string, component_class: string, parent_binding_guid?: string, binding_guid: string, display_name: string, component_bound: bool, parented_to_actor: bool, possessable_count: int, property_name?: string, property_type?: string, track_class?: string, section_class?: string, saved: bool, save_error?: string } -- the property fields only when a track was added.`

## `create_cine_camera_in_sequence`

*Additive.*

Creates a spawnable CineCameraActor binding, keys its transform, and binds a camera cut to it.  High-value one-shot: spawnable CineCameraActor + transform track keyed at frame 0 + a camera cut spanning the playback range.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `location` | array | no | Optional [x, y, z] world location for the camera's key at frame 0. |
| `rotation` | array | no | Optional [pitch, yaw, roll] world rotation for the camera's key at frame 0. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, display_name: string, class_name: string, spawnable: bool, transform_keyed: bool, camera_cut_added: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `create_level_sequence`

*Destructive.*

Creates a Level Sequence asset at package_path/sequence_name and saves it, with playback range [0, duration) and frame_rate, truncated to whole fps, as both tick resolution and display rate; the end frame is duration times that whole rate, to the nearest frame. If that asset already exists it is loaded and those settings are overwritten, its keys, sections and ranges migrated to the new rate so nothing moves in time; sequence_created tells a new asset from an existing one. Not undoable; another asset class at the path, or a duration shorter than one frame, is an error. To retime an existing sequence use set_sequence_frame_rate or set_sequence_playback_range (duration); list sequences with get_level_sequences.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the new sequence to create |
| `package_path` | string | no | Target content path, defaults to /Game/Sequences |
| `duration` | number | no | Playback duration in seconds, above 0 and at most 3600, default 10 |
| `frame_rate` | number | no | Frame rate in fps, at least 1 and at most 120, truncated to whole fps, default 30 |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, package_path: string, duration: number, frame_rate: number, sequence_created: bool (false when the asset already existed), saved: bool, asset_path: string, playback_range_set: bool, tick_rate_set: bool, actual_start_frame: int, actual_end_frame: int }`

## `duplicate_keyframe`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Copy the value of one existing key to another time on a property track of a Level Sequence binding, in one undo step, then save the sequence. The sequence is found by asset name under /Game (first case-insensitive match); property_type picks the binding's first track of that type (first section) and channel_index the channel, one per component for Vector and Color. Both times are seconds rounded to tick frames, and the source key must sit exactly on its frame or the call is an error. Only the value is copied, not interpolation or tangents; a key at the destination is overwritten, one equal to the copy is a no-op (changed false, saved false), so a repeat is idempotent. A failed save gives success false, saved=false and save_error. Move instead: move_keyframe; drop: remove_keyframe; list: get_channel_keyframes; fix the copy's interpolation: set_binding_channel_keyframe_interpolation.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding owning the property track. |
| `property_type` | string | yes | One of "Float", "Bool", "Vector", "Color", "Visibility". |
| `source_time_seconds` | number | yes | Time (seconds) of the source key to copy. |
| `dest_time_seconds` | number | yes | Destination time (seconds) for the cloned key. |
| `channel_index` | number | no | Index of the channel to read/write (default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, binding_guid: string, property_type: string, source_time_seconds: float, dest_time_seconds: float, source_frame: int, dest_frame: int, channel_index: int, duplicated_value: string, keys_written: int, applied: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `get_audio_section_properties`

*Read-only.*

Read the playback settings of one audio section of a Level Sequence (path or bare name): the first root audio track, section by section_index. Use it instead of get_properties because it evaluates what no UPROPERTY holds directly: volume and pitch sampled at frame 0, the key counts of the animated volume/pitch channels, and looping via IsRepeating(); it also reports sound, start offset and attenuation override. Pure reader (no transaction, no save); write with set_audio_section_properties.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the Level Sequence that owns the (root) audio track. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the resolved root audio track (default 0). |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, section_class: string, section_index: int, sound_path: string, start_offset: int, volume: number, pitch: number, volume_key_count: int, pitch_key_count: int, looping: bool, play_until_finished?: bool (needs UE 5.8), suppress_subtitles: bool, override_attenuation: bool, attenuation_path: string }`

## `get_channel_keyframes`

*Read-only.*

Read every keyframe on one channel of a binding's section (resolved like set_section_easing).  Pure reader (no transaction/save).  channel_type selects which channel proxy view to index: "double" (transform loc/rot/scale, default), "float" (property/color), "bool" (visibility).  Bool keys omit interp/tangent fields.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding whose section to read. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `track_type` | string | no | Optional class filter (see set_section_easing) selecting the track on the binding. |
| `track_index` | number | no | Index into the binding's tracks (default 0; used when track_type omitted). |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0). |
| `channel_type` | string | no | Channel value kind: "double" (default) \| "float" \| "bool". |
| `channel_index` | number | no | Index of the channel within its proxy view (default 0). |
| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, channel_index: int, channel_type: string, key_count: int, keyframes: [{ index: int, frame: int, time_seconds: number, value: number|bool, interp_mode: string, tangent_mode: string, arrive_tangent: number, leave_tangent: number }] }`

## `get_sequence_bindings`

*Read-only.*

Lists the object bindings of a Level Sequence, the first asset under /Game whose name matches sequence_name (case-insensitive), with each binding's bound class, parent GUID, spawn ownership and tracks (class, display name, section count, is_empty); read-only, needs no open Sequencer. kind narrows it to possessables or spawnables, binding_guid to one binding. spawnable is true when the binding has a spawn track (a spawnable is recorded as a possessable plus a spawn track) and possessable otherwise; possessable_count and spawnable_count are the movie scene's own counts and can disagree with those flags. Root tracks are not listed: use get_sequence_tracks. Change a spawnable's ownership with set_spawn_ownership; one section's range, easing and blend come from get_section_info.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `kind` | string | no | Optional 'all' (default), 'possessable' or 'spawnable' (case-insensitive): which bindings to list. |
| `binding_guid` | string | no | Optional GUID of one binding to list alone; an invalid GUID, or one the sequence has no binding for, is an error. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, kind: string, binding_guid?: string, bindings: [{guid, name, spawnable, possessable, class, parent_guid, spawn_ownership, track_count, tracks: [{class, display_name, section_count, is_empty}]}], binding_count: int, possessable_count: int, spawnable_count: int } -- class is the bound (or spawned) actor class, "null" when unknown; parent_guid is "" for a top-level binding; spawn_ownership (InnerSequence, RootSequence or External) is "" unless the binding is a spawnable custom binding.`

## `get_sequence_folders`

*Read-only.*

Read the Sequencer folder tree of a Level Sequence (root folders, recursively, with child tracks + bindings). Read-only.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, root_folder_count: int, folders: [{ name: string, child_folders: [...recursive...], child_tracks: [{class, name}], child_bindings: [guid_string] }] }`

## `get_sequence_tracks`

*Read-only.*

Lists the tracks of a Level Sequence, given as a bare asset name (the first asset under /Game whose name matches, case-insensitive) or a /Game path: root (master) tracks, the camera cut track included, with display name, track name, class and section count, then each object binding (guid, display name) with its own tracks nested, plus totals -- track counts, section count and a per-class breakdown. Read-only; needs no open Sequencer. total_track_count is the number of tracks listed: root tracks plus every binding's tracks. For spawnable/possessable flags and one binding's tracks use get_sequence_bindings.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target level sequence, or its /Game path |
| `sequence_path` | string | no | Alias of sequence_name |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, sequence_path: string, master_tracks: [{display_name, track_name, class, section_count}], bindings: [{guid, display_name, tracks: [{display_name, track_name, class, section_count}]}], master_track_count: int, binding_count: int, binding_track_count: int, total_track_count: int, total_section_count: int, distinct_class_count: int, class_breakdown: [{class, count}] } -- class_breakdown counts every listed track by class, most frequent first.`

## `get_timeline_info`

*Read-only.*

Reads the timeline summary of a Level Sequence asset (first asset-name match under /Game); needs no open Sequencer and changes nothing. Returns asset_path, start_frame and end_frame in ticks (the playback range), duration in seconds, tick_resolution and display_rate each with numerator and denominator, and track, binding, possessable and spawnable counts. master_track_count counts the root tracks, the camera cut track included, as get_sequence_tracks lists them.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name of the Level Sequence, not its path (e.g. "LS_Intro"); the first match under /Game is used |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, asset_path: string, start_frame: int, end_frame: int, duration: number, tick_resolution: number, tick_resolution_numerator: int, tick_resolution_denominator: int, display_rate: number, display_rate_numerator: int, display_rate_denominator: int, master_track_count: int, binding_count: int, possessable_count: int, spawnable_count: int } -- start_frame/end_frame are tick-resolution frames, not display frames; tick_resolution is the rate set_sequence_frame_rate changes together with display_rate.`

## `move_keyframe`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Move one key of a channel of one section on an object-binding track of a Level Sequence to new_frame, keeping its value, interpolation and tangents, in one undo step, then save the sequence. The key is found by index, or by frame within tolerance; channel_type (double, float or bool) and channel_index pick the channel, and the section is resolved like get_section_info. Another key already at new_frame is removed, so a repeat call is idempotent. A key already alone at new_frame changes and saves nothing (changed false, saved false), with moved false. A missing key or channel is an error before anything changes. Remove a key: remove_keyframe; list keys: get_channel_keyframes.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Full /Game path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `binding_guid` | string | yes | GUID of the binding whose section to edit. |
| `new_frame` | number | yes | Destination frame number for the key. |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `track_type` | string | no | Optional class filter (see set_section_easing) selecting the track on the binding. |
| `track_index` | number | no | Index into the binding's tracks (default 0; used when track_type omitted). |
| `section_index` | number | no | Index of the section on the resolved track (default 0). |
| `channel_type` | string | no | Channel value kind: "double" (default) \| "float" \| "bool". |
| `channel_index` | number | no | Index of the channel within its proxy view (default 0). |
| `index` | integer | no | Index of the key to move (mutually exclusive with frame). |
| `frame` | integer | no | Frame of the key to move (resolved via FindKey; provide index OR frame). |
| `tolerance` | integer | no | Optional FindKey frame tolerance when locating by frame (default 0). |
| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, channel_index: int, channel_type: string, old_frame: int, new_frame: int, key_index: int, moved: bool, changed: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string, note?: string }`

## `move_track_to_folder`

*Destructive, idempotent.*

Move a master track (by class) or an object-binding (by GUID) into a named Sequencer folder, inside an undo transaction, and save the sequence; success requires the save. Idempotent: a track or binding already in the folder succeeds with already_present true and saved false (nothing is written).

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_path` | string | yes | Asset path OR bare asset name of the target Level Sequence. |
| `folder_name` | string | yes | Name of the destination folder (searched recursively). |
| `sequence_name` | string | no | Alias for sequence_path. |
| `track_class` | string | no | Class name of the master track to move (e.g. "MovieSceneCameraCutTrack"). Mutually exclusive with binding_guid. |
| `track_name` | string | no | Optional track name to disambiguate when several tracks share the class. |
| `binding_guid` | string | no | GUID of an object-binding to move into the folder. Mutually exclusive with track_class. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, folder_name: string, track_class: string, track_name: string, binding_guid: string, moved: bool, already_present: bool, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

*Destructive.*

Pauses, at its current position, the runtime ULevelSequencePlayer whose player_key play_level_sequence_runtime returned. Players live in the PIE or game world and stop resolving once it ends. Returns player_key, paused, playing and current_time in seconds; read it later with get_level_sequence_status_runtime.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `player_key` | string | yes | Player key returned from play_level_sequence_runtime |

**Returns:** `{ player_key: string, paused: bool, playing: bool, current_time: number }`

## `pause_timeline`

*Destructive.*

Pause playback in the open Sequencer editor on a target sequence

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, playing: bool, paused: bool }`

## `play_level_sequence_runtime`

*Additive.*

Spawn an ALevelSequenceActor with a ULevelSequencePlayer for a Level Sequence in a running PIE or game world, start it with default playback settings, and return the player_key the other runtime tools take. Every call makes a new player and actor with its own key, even for a sequence already playing; nothing in the editor level or on disk changes. No PIE or game world, a world selector naming the editor world, or no sequence of that name under /Game is an error and nothing is spawned. The key stops resolving when PIE ends. Then: pause_level_sequence_runtime, set_level_sequence_time_runtime, get_level_sequence_status_runtime, and stop_level_sequence_runtime to release the player and destroy its actor; to scrub in the editor without PIE, play_timeline or set_timeline_time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Asset name of the Level Sequence, not its path, e.g. "LS_Intro"; matched case-insensitively, and the first match under /Game is used. |
| `world` | string | no | Optional world selector: absent/'pie' (default: PlayWorld, else the first PIE context) \| 'server' \| 'client' \| 'pie:N' \| 'game' (alias of 'pie'). Runtime playback needs a PIE/Game world (an editor world has no movie-scene tick manager and would assert), so an editor world is refused here. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, player_key: string, playing: bool, current_time: number, world: string, world_name: string|null, world_package: string|null, world_type: string|null, net_mode: string|null, pie_instance: number }`

## `play_timeline`

*Additive, idempotent.*

Starts playback in the editor's Sequencer on a Level Sequence found by asset name under /Game, first opening it there when it is not the sequence shown. Editor preview only, no PIE or game player (use play_level_sequence_runtime for that). Returns at once and changes no asset; calling it while playing keeps playing. playing is read right after the call. Errors when the sequence is missing or no Sequencer can show it. Pause with pause_timeline; move the playhead with set_timeline_time.

| Parameter | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence_name` | string | yes | Name of the target level sequence |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_name: string, playing: bool }`

| `channel_type` | string | no | Channel value kind: "double" (default) \| "float" \| "bool". |
| `channel_index` | number | no | Index of the channel within its proxy view (default 0). |
| `index` | integer | no | Index of the key to remove (mutually exclusive with frame). |
| `frame` | integer | no | Frame of the key to remove (resolved via FindKey; provide index OR frame). |

| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |

**Returns:** `{ sequence_path: string, channel_type: string, channel_index: int, removed_frame: int, key_index: int, removed: bool, key_count_after: int, saved: bool, save_error?: string }`

## `remove_marked_frame`

*Destructive.*

Removes one user marked frame from a Level Sequence, by index, frame, or label -- or, with all=true, every marked frame -- inside an undo transaction, and saves the sequence; success requires the save. A selector that matches no mark, or all=true on a sequence without marks, succeeds with already_removed true and saved false (nothing is written).

Remove a section from a sequencer track by index.  Resolves the section like set_section_active (binding_guid + track_type/index + section_index), then removes it from its owning track via UMovieSceneTrack::RemoveSectionAt. One delete for what every per-track add_*_section adds.

| `binding_name_or_guid` | string | no | Alias for binding_guid, read only when binding_guid is absent; it must also be a GUID string, a bound object's name is not resolved. |

## `remove_sequence_binding`

*Destructive.*

Remove a spawnable or possessable binding, found by GUID, from a Level Sequence named by asset name under /Game, then save the sequence; a failed save returns success false. Fails when the GUID is not a spawnable or possessable of the sequence. Returns removed_as; get GUIDs from get_sequence_bindings.
